page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-64 is a high-density compute-focused instance within Google Cloud's virtual machine catalog. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server provisions 64 dedicated virtual CPU cores paired with 120 GB of system memory. With a memory-to-core allocation of 1.88 GB per vCPU, the configuration emphasizes raw parallel processing capacity over expansive RAM sizing, serving operations where CPU concurrency is the primary operational driver.

The instance does not include bundled local disk storage and contains zero GPU accelerators. Data persistence and file system operations require network-attached block storage volumes. The absence of local NVMe storage aligns with stateless and horizontally scalable architectures, although workloads that demand ultra-low local storage latency must accommodate network storage overhead.

In terms of resource efficiency, the c4d-highcpu-64 provides an advantageous profile for CPU-dominated deployments. By curtailing the RAM allocation relative to balanced general-purpose types, deployments avoid paying for unused memory allocations. The primary operational tradeoff is the lower memory-per-core ratio, which constrains execution of memory-heavy databases or caching infrastructure.

Given its substantial core count and targeted memory configuration, the instance fits parallel computing workloads. Recommended deployments include continuous integration and automated build pipelines, batch data processing, distributed microservices, media transcoding, and compute-intensive scientific simulations.
